worksheets.title: Grouped Histograms, Back-to-Back Stem Plots, and Quartiles

fluency_questions.prompt: Find the minimum, median ($Q_2$), and maximum for each ordered list:
Find $Q_1$, $Q_3$, and $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$ for each ordered list of $7$ scores (exclude the middle score $Q_2$ first):
Put each list in ascending order first, then find the range ($\text{Max} - \text{Min}$) and median:
A grouped table of $20$ test marks has intervals: $0\text{--}<10$ ($f=2$), $10\text{--}<20$ ($f=5$), $20\text{--}<30$ ($f=9$), $30\text{--}<40$ ($f=4$). Answer:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Which interval is the modal class (highest frequency)?

parts.label: b
parts.question: How many students scored less than $20$?

parts.label: c
parts.question: What percentage of students scored less than $20$?

parts.label: d
parts.question: What is the midpoint of the interval $20\text{--}<30$?

application_questions.question: Two netball shooters record their goals per game: Player A has median $18$ and $\text{IQR} = 4$; Player B has median $18$ and $\text{IQR} = 11$. Which player is more consistent?
application_questions.answer: Player A, because her $\text{IQR}$ ($4$) is much smaller than Player B's ($11$).

application_questions.question: A stem-and-leaf plot has key $4 \mid 3 = 43$. Write down the numbers represented by stem $3$ with leaves $1, 4, 7$.
Five houses in a street sell for $\$500\text{k}, \$520\text{k}, \$540\text{k}, \$560\text{k}, \$2000\text{k}$. Find the median house price.
A school surveys only students waiting at the tuckshop about whether the tuckshop needs more seating. Why might this sample be biased?
application_questions.answer: It uses convenience sampling of tuckshop customers only, ignoring students who bring lunch from home.

reasoning_questions.question: Why must you always sort numbers from smallest to largest before finding $Q_1, Q_2$, and $Q_3$?
reasoning_questions.answer: Because quartiles and the median depend on position in an ordered list; an unsorted list gives meaningless positions.

reasoning_questions.question: On the left side of a back-to-back stem plot, why do the leaves grow outwards from right to left?
reasoning_questions.answer: So that the smallest digits sit closest to the central stem on both sides, keeping the plot symmetric around the stem.

application_questions.question: A student plots study hours ($x$) against test score ($y$). Which variable goes on the horizontal axis?
A line of best fit for plant height $h$ (cm) after $w$ weeks ($1 \le w \le 10$) is $h = 3w + 5$. Predict the height after $6$ weeks.
In a survey, $24$ out of $40$ boys ($60\%$) and $15$ out of $50$ girls ($30\%$) play video games daily. Which group has the higher rate?
A school has $100$ Year 7 students and $200$ Year 8 students ($300$ total). How many Year 7 students should be in a fair stratified sample of $30$ students?

reasoning_questions.question: Why is predicting outside the range of your data (extrapolation) risky?
reasoning_questions.answer: Because the trend might curve, level off, or stop making physical sense outside the observed data.

reasoning_questions.question: Ice-cream sales and sunburn cases both rise in summer. Does eating ice cream cause sunburn? Explain.
reasoning_questions.answer: No; hot sunny weather is a third lurking variable that causes both more ice-cream sales and more sunburn.
